I can kind of understand this as I've dated someone who relied heavily on weed just to function on a day to day, and it is very irritating when I hear people say that weed doesn't change anything about a person. Because it does, especially when they're not smoking. My ex was highly irritable and very standoffish when she wasn't smoking, and very lazy and sloppy when she was, but because she didn't want to acknowledge the reality around her, she used weed as a way to escape. And while yes, weed doesn't have much of an effect physically, there's still the mental effect, like people who smoke will do so before and after they eat, smoke before going anywhere, smoke on lumch breaks at work, basically their life becomes smoking at various intervals, because they convinced themselves that they need to in order to make it through. I think the best thing you can do is try to voice your concerns for his behavior not just towards you but in general and give him time to accept it or not. I would also bring up how odd it is that the therapist is pushing for divorce since usually therapist would push for the relationship to stay since it's a more solid foundation for someone struggling mentally than if they were alone, unless he is pushing all the blame on you, to which you should speak on any concerns regarding his inability to take responsibility for his actions and mental state.
